beats.narration_en: Same speed, same sudden stop. Only the gap is different.
When the car ahead brakes, you don't. Not yet.
Your brain needs about one and a half seconds to see it and hit the pedal.
At sixty miles an hour that's over forty yards before you even touch the brake.
Then the brakes need room too, and that room grows with the square of your speed.
Double your speed and you need four times the distance to stop.
The car ahead stops in forty six meters. You need eighty six.
So count three seconds after the car ahead passes a sign.
If you reach the sign before you get to three, you're too close.
And a two second look at your phone at sixty is more than fifty yards driven blind.
The gap is the only thing that buys you that time.
